content:
Alex R: Quick sync — we need a compact playbook for picking quant profiles for incoming models (intake -> select int8/fp8/gguf -> calibration -> rollouts). Starting list of constraints: latency SLO, token cost delta target, quality delta budget (per-metric). Thoughts?

Maria G: +1. Suggest separating profiles by workload: generation-chat, L2R-completion, embeddings, rerank. Each has different sensitivity.

Jong Kim: For the new 30B LLaMA-variant: my rule: try parametric int8 (GGUF) first for cost cut ~2.5x. If >1.5% RLHF-judge regression or >2% ppl increase, fallback to mixed fp8. Also run sensitivity sweep with 256 calibration samples covering long-tail prompts.

Samir: Checklist:
- smoke eval (10 prompts)
- quick sensitivity sweep (100–500 samples)
- full evalset (1k)
- latency/cost bench (batch sizes + seq lengths)
- canary rollout 5% -> 20% -> 100% with automated rollback
- monitor token-level cost and per-route quality

Maria G: Command I use:
```
./tools/run_quant_sweep --model path/to/model.gguf --calib ./data/calib.jsonl --sweep int8,fp8,hybrid --seed 42 --save profiles/
```
Outputs a csv with metrics and per-prompt deltas.

Eva (ci-bot): sensitivity-run 1976543225: finished. top candidates:
- gguf-int8-v1 (ppl +1.4%, rouge -0.8, latency -42%, cost -2.8x)
- fp8-symmetric-v2 (ppl +0.6%, rouge -0.2, latency -25%, cost -1.9x)

Alex R: Nice — we should codify gating thresholds: ppl delta <=1.0% OR task-specific metric delta <=0.5% -> promote int8; else if ppl <=1.5% and latency gain >30% -> consider fp8 hybrid; else keep fp16.

Jong Kim: Calib dataset: at least 500 samples drawn 70/30 short/long, with adversarial tail prompts (rare tokens, long context). Use temperature variety and include generation stop-length extremes.

Samir: Telemetry keys to add: quant_profile, calibration_seed, eval_set_id, metric_deltas, canary_percent. Canary policy: 5% for 12h -> check regression alerts -> 20% for 24h -> full. Automated rollback on >1% task-metric regression.

Maria G: Naming conv: <model>-<profile>-<precision>-v<semver> e.g. llama30b-gguf-int8-v1

Alex R: I'm happy to own first run for llama30b-custx. I'll kick off after lunch. Who can review artifacts + eval?

Jong Kim: I'll review evals.

Samir: I'll set up canary policies and dashboards.

Alex R: Thanks everyone :rocket:
